account:
Today my scheduled business has mostly proceeded without new council correspondence, but several matters remain unresolved. I attended the mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection and could not locate the miller or obtain grain quantities or storage records. I therefore recorded the inspection as incomplete rather than claiming that supplies or conditions were satisfactory. The secretary has secured my report and will check tomorrow's appointments before proposing a ten o'clock follow-up with the miller and records present.

There is unusual talk about a bridge or port change associated with the bakery. Townsfolk repeated it, naming the baker, innkeeper and neighbour as people who had been there. This is hearsay: I have seen no actual proposal, and the secretary has received none. I do not yet know whether it concerns a genuine change, a misunderstanding, or merely gossip.

There is also activity around the great hall. An eighteen hundred lighting inspection with the builder has been confirmed and recorded by the secretary. The baker came to the office seeking confirmation after hearing about it from freight, and reported that his eighty contracted loaves had been delivered to the hall. That suggests preparations involving hall use, but I do not know the occasion or whether the bread delivery and lighting inspection serve the same purpose. I have not personally checked the delivery.

I have now reached the dockside cottage for my fifteen hundred tea, somewhat late, and can see my neighbour nearby. This appears to be our usual social appointment. I still have my sixteen-thirty office appointment, eighteen hundred lighting inspection and nineteen hundred return home to keep.
